tooltip: State School Fund: the main source of state money for K-12 school districts
definition: The primary source of state funding for Oregon's K-12 school districts. Districts use it to pay educator salaries, buy textbooks and maintain schools. The Legislature sets the amount for each two-year budget.

tooltip: Current service level: what it costs to keep existing programs going for the next two years
definition: The amount estimated to be needed to continue currently approved programs and services for the next two-year budget, using standard inflation assumptions. Budget writers start from it. For schools, the Department of Administrative Services calculates the State School Fund CSL: its figure in the 2026 QEM report, including the Student Success Act transfer, is $12.56 billion for 2027-29.

tooltip: Quality Education Model: the state's estimate of what Oregon schools need to meet the quality goals in law
definition: The state's own estimate of what it costs for Oregon's schools to meet the quality goals set in law. The Quality Education Commission updates it and publishes a report every two years, in August of even-numbered years. It prices two levels: the status quo (today's services) and the full QEM (what's needed to meet the goals). See "status quo QEM" and "full QEM" below. The JPEA has criticized how the model is built. A JPEA proposal to move the cost model out of the Quality Education Commission became SB 1555 (2026), described by its sponsor as replacing the QEM; news reports say that overhaul effort was unsuccessful.

tooltip: Quality Education Commission: the state commission that produces the Quality Education Model
definition: The commission the Legislature created in statute in 2001 to define the cost of meeting Oregon's quality goals for schools. It updates and publishes the Quality Education Model.

full_name: Joint Committee on Public Education Appropriation
tooltip: Joint Committee on Public Education Appropriation: reports whether the Legislature's school funding is sufficient
definition: The legislative committee that reports whether the state's school funding is sufficient to meet the quality goals in law. If it isn't, the report must say by how much and what that means for schools. By law it relies on the Quality Education Commission's findings.

tooltip: Education Stability Fund: a state reserve whose withdrawals must go to public education
definition: One of Oregon's two general reserve accounts; the other is the Rainy Day Fund. It took its current structure through a 2002 constitutional amendment and receives 18% of Lottery earnings. Withdrawals need a three-fifths vote in each chamber plus either an economic trigger or a governor's emergency declaration, and must be used for public education.

tooltip: Office of Economic Analysis: the state's economic and revenue forecasters
definition: The state's economists, part of the Department of Administrative Services, who publish the Oregon Economic and Revenue Forecast. The forecast tells budget writers how much money the state expects to have. In this archive OEA always means this office; the teachers' union (Oregon Education Association) is written out in full.

tooltip: Department of Administrative Services: state agency that houses the revenue forecasters and calculates the State School Fund CSL
definition: A state agency. It houses the Office of Economic Analysis and calculates the State School Fund current service level used in the Quality Education Model report.

tooltip: Legislative Fiscal Office: the Legislature's budget office
definition: The Legislature's budget office. Its staff prepare budget documents for the Joint Committee on Ways and Means and publish Budget Highlights summarizing each adopted budget.

tooltip: Legislative Revenue Office: the Legislature's revenue office
definition: The Legislature's revenue office. After each session, the Office of Economic Analysis builds LRO's estimates of how new laws change revenue into the state forecast. LRO also publishes summaries of the state's reserve funds.

tooltip: Oregon Department of Revenue
definition: The state agency that publishes A Brief History of Oregon Property Taxation, the source this archive uses for Measures 5 and 50. It also assesses some property, such as public utilities and large industrial plants.

tooltip: Oregon Department of Education: the state's K-12 education agency
definition: The state agency for K-12 education. It supports the Quality Education Commission's work and carries out orders such as the Governor's instructional-time executive order.

tooltip: Student Success Act: 2019 law expected to invest over $2 billion in education every two years
definition: A 2019 law, funded by the Corporate Activities Act passed the same year, expected to invest over $2 billion in Oregon education every two years. About $700 million of that goes into the State School Fund (the "SSA transfer"); the rest goes to three other accounts.

tooltip: Public Employees Retirement System: the state pension system school districts pay into
definition: The retirement system that school districts and education service districts pay into for their employees' pensions. The PERS Board approves employer contribution rates in the fall of even-numbered years.

tooltip: Individualized Education Program: a plan of services for a student with a disability
definition: A plan that promises a student with a disability specific educational services, under the federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act. Meeting those needs generally costs more than for other students.

tooltip: Executive order issued by the Governor
definition: An order issued by the Governor. For example, EO 26-06 directs ODE to ask the State Board of Education for emergency rules that preserve student instructional time.

tooltip: Senate Bill
definition: A bill introduced in the Oregon Senate, followed by its number (e.g. SB 141).

tooltip: House Bill
definition: A bill introduced in the Oregon House, followed by its number (e.g. HB 2767 of 2023).

tooltip: Oregon Legislative Information System: the Legislature's site for bills and committee documents
definition: The Legislature's online system where bills and committee meeting documents are posted. Many documents in this archive come from it.

tooltip: Oregon School Boards Association
definition: An Oregon organization of school boards. This archive treats its documents as advocacy material and labels its figures as its own estimates.

tooltip: Coalition of Oregon School Administrators
definition: An Oregon organization of school administrators. This archive treats its documents as advocacy material and labels its figures as its own estimates.

tooltip: Portland Public Schools
definition: The Portland school district. Its own documents are kept in a separate PPS research archive.

full_name: Joint Committee on Ways and Means
tooltip: Ways and Means: the Legislature's joint budget committee
definition: Short for the Joint Committee on Ways and Means, the Legislature's joint budget committee. See "Ways and Means" below.

tooltip: Governor's Recommended Budget: the Governor's proposed two-year budget, normally due Dec 1 of even-numbered years
definition: Short for the Governor's Recommended Budget. See "Governor's Recommended Budget" below.
A two-year budget period. Oregon budgets two years at a time; 2027-29 is the next one. The state constitution requires the Legislature to fund schools sufficiently "in each biennium".

full_name: Status Quo Core K-12 State Funding
definition: The Quality Education Model's estimate of what it costs to maintain the current activities of Oregon's K-12 schools: $13.78 billion in state funding for 2027-29. It counts funding sources beyond the State School Fund, so it is higher than the SSF current service level. This site calls it "keep today's services".

The Quality Education Model's estimate of what it costs to keep current services and add the investments needed to improve student outcomes: $16.21 billion in state funding for 2027-29. This site calls it "meet the state's goals".

The difference between what the Quality Education Model says is needed and what the state funds. The constitution requires the Legislature to report the extent of any such shortfall and its impact on meeting the quality goals.
Oregon's other general reserve account besides the Education Stability Fund, created in 2007. Withdrawals can't exceed two-thirds of its balance at the start of the biennium; the ESF has no such cap.

Oregon's law that returns income tax surpluses to taxpayers when actual collections beat the forecast by 2% or more over a two-year budget. The Legislative Fiscal Office says it made building reserves more challenging. Corporate taxes have their own kicker threshold and are handled separately: the December 2026 forecast puts corporate taxes just above it, which would dedicate $71 million to education spending in 2027-29 if the forecast holds.

The Governor's proposed two-year state budget. By law it goes to legislators no later than December 1 of each even-numbered year (Dec 1, 2026 for 2027-29), with an exception for years when a new Governor takes office the following January. The Legislature then writes the final budget.

full_name: Joint Committee on Ways and Means
definition: The Legislature's joint budget committee. Its Education Subcommittee takes up the State School Fund budget bill, working from Legislative Fiscal Office recommendations (for 2025-27, SB 5516).
A 1990 ballot measure that introduced limits on property tax rates. Fully in effect by 1995-96, it cut tax rates an average of 51% from 1990-91 levels.
A 1997 ballot measure that cut property taxes, limited growth in assessed value and replaced most tax levies with permanent tax rates.

tooltip: ADMr: a school's or district's resident student count, unweighted
definition: Average daily membership of resident students: the unweighted student count the state uses, for example in its budget projections. For charter students it is counted in the district where the charter is located.

tooltip: ADMw: student count with extra weight for students who cost more to serve, used to split the State School Fund
definition: Weighted average daily membership: the student count with added weights (for example for special education, English learners and poverty) that the State School Fund formula uses to divide money among districts.

The higher of a district's current or prior year's ADMw. The State School Fund formula uses it as a hold-harmless for districts whose enrollment is falling. For a sponsor whose own enrollment fell, a virtual charter's ADMw is calculated separately.

The main part of a district's State School Fund formula amount, before transportation and before local revenue is subtracted. ODE prints each district's grant and grant per extended ADMw on its estimate pages. Charter pass-through minimums are set as a share of the sponsor's grant per ADMw.

tooltip: Student Investment Account: Student Success Act grants to districts; virtual charters can't apply
definition: A grant account created by the Student Success Act. Virtual public charter schools are not eligible to apply, and ODE removes their ADMw from their sponsors' allocations.

tooltip: Legislative Policy and Research Office: the Legislature's policy research staff
definition: The Legislature's research office. Its analysts write staff measure summaries and session summary reports.

tooltip: Oregon Revised Statutes: Oregon's codified state laws
definition: The codified laws of Oregon, published by chapter (for example chapter 338, public charter schools).

tooltip: Oregon Journalism Project: a news organization whose investigation of online schools ran in Willamette Week
definition: A news organization. Its Nov 2026 investigation of Oregon's online schools was published in Willamette Week.
